title: CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md and keeps only a short harness addendum
description:
The target architecture (docs/architecture/target-architecture.md, §5.1 layer H6 and §12 step M0) keeps the harness adapters thin, because instruction files cost the agent context in every session: CLAUDE.md is an import of AGENTS.md plus a harness-specific addendum of at most 200 lines. Today CLAUDE.md does not import AGENTS.md — it points to it in prose and then carries the block `bd init` generated, whose quick reference names bare `bd` commands where the house rules require the pinned wrapper (tools/bd). The review of the corpus against the running workflow recorded the missing import.

What: CLAUDE.md starts with the import of AGENTS.md; the addendum holds only what is specific to Claude Code; the generated Beads block is either reduced to a pointer to `tools/bd prime` or kept below the import with its commands routed through tools/bd — decided in the change, with the reason in the pull request. Prerequisite of Omnigent step M0 (coding-harness-eev).
acceptance_criteria:
- CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md on its first content line.
- CLAUDE.md is at most 200 lines, and no command in it bypasses tools/bd.
- A test checks the import and the line limit.

title: Omnigent step M0: proof of concept in a throwaway repository (D-7)
description:
Decided 2026-09-16 (target architecture, docs/architecture/target-architecture.md, §9.1 D-7 and §12): the Omnigent migration plan is the main path, steps M0 to M4 in order, starting now. M0 proves that the Omnigent server can host agent sessions without weakening the git-native gates, in a throwaway repository.

What:
- An Omnigent server on a dedicated machine: version pinned with a deliberate upgrade step, telemetry opt-out as the first configuration step, the OSS variant, no employer account.
- The approval boundaries as server policies, each proven to fire on a known-bad case before it counts.
- A Beads task loop — claim, implement, commit, close — inside a sandboxed session in the throwaway repository.
- A blocked session observed from a second device.
- The tmux fallback topology rehearsed once.

Non-negotiable: the server holds no state that the repository and the tracker do not also hold; no model call to an endpoint that model-endpoints.yaml does not declare (RB-A6).

Harness prerequisites, tracked as dependencies: the gate file with its verify command and the export writer of D-4 (coding-harness-bo0); the red mechanism tests resolved by class (coding-harness-2ee); the worktree verification of D-5 (coding-harness-m34); CLAUDE.md importing AGENTS.md (coding-harness-21f).

Abort or hold: the sandbox does not work on the target machine; bd is unreliable inside Omnigent terminals; alpha instability interrupts the proof of concept more than once a day. Then stay on the fallback topology and keep the harness prerequisites.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every basis policy fires on its known-bad case; the protocol is in the repository.
- One full task loop runs without manual intervention beyond approvals.
- The telemetry opt-out is shown by observing egress.
- The same loop is repeated once in the fallback topology.

title: Verify tracker writes from worktrees before lifting the write ban (D-5)
description:
Decided 2026-09-16 (target architecture, docs/architecture/target-architecture.md, §9.1 D-5): worktrees live inside the repository through each tool's own mechanism — .claude/worktrees/ through Claude Code, `bd worktree create` elsewhere — based fresh on the remote default branch; hand-made sibling directories are retired. Until this verification is green, no session writes to the tracker from a worktree: beads are created, updated and closed in the main checkout only.

What: in a throwaway repository with its own tracker and its own remote, using the pinned bd (tools/beads/VERSION), run the verification the toolchain document prescribes before stage 2 (docs/research/Lake-Switch-Architektur-arc42.md, §5.2.6), plus a fifth check:
1. An agent in a worktree sees the same `bd list` as the main checkout.
2. The environment variables that locate the tracker and name the agent's role arrive inside the worktree session (including a sandboxed session, where variables must be declared to pass through).
3. `bd create` in the worktree produces a bead that is visible in the main checkout.
4. Two worktrees claim and write at the same time without losing or corrupting a write.
5. Beads created from a worktree carry the full configured id prefix, not a shortened one — the defect reproduced in portfolio on 2026-09-16 in a worktree and in its main checkout (tracked there as wp-p0.1).
acceptance_criteria:
- A protocol with commands and results of all five checks is committed in this repository.
- Either the write ban lifts by a sentence in AGENTS.md, or it stays with the failing check named and the fallback chosen.

title: Template bundle for M1: spec with class and Definition of Done, design phase, architecture templates
description:
Re-scoped 2026-09-17. The original slice — templates/ and the handover schema script moved from portfolio — landed with the mechanism adoption (Phase 3, commit 5efe809). What remains is the template bundle that the target architecture names as a prerequisite of Omnigent step M1 (docs/architecture/target-architecture.md, §5.1 layer H3 and §12).

Contents:
- A spec template. It carries the contract prompt 02 already requires (goal, acceptance criteria, non-goals) plus `class` as a frontmatter field with four values — Spike, Bounded, Feature, Architectural (D-12) — protected areas, failure mode, size, and a Definition of Done section (D-2). The Definition of Done holds only what is specific to the change: documents, models and ADRs that must move in the same pull request; non-goals asserted untouched; which bead closes with which trailer; special runs. For the gates it holds exactly one line, "`verify` green", never a list (O-1). Prompt 02 references the template.
- The design phase 2b: a prompt (prompts/02b-design.md) and a design.md template with alternatives and their consequences, interfaces, data model, an ADR draft and the model-as-code delta. Mandatory for Architectural, optional for Feature with a one-sentence reason in spec.md, absent for Bounded and Spike (D-14).
- The findings and plan-marking templates moved from portfolio: WORKFLOW.md links to both, and neither exists in this repository.
- A ROADMAP.md template, an arc42 skeleton and a MADR decision record.
- templates/architecture/ with a LikeC4 specification that pins the four C4 element kinds — system, container, component, code (D-15).

Not in this item: the validator rules that check class, Definition of Done and the design artefact (the presence validator becomes a mechanism entry, D-11); the per-instance model routing file with its schema (D-16); the machine-rendered verification report.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every template listed above exists under templates/ (and the 2b prompt under prompts/).
- Every template link in WORKFLOW.md resolves.
- The kit manifest lists the new files with their role.
- The Leerprobe number does not drop against the measurement before the change.

title: Gate file and one verify command; ci.yml derived from it (D-10)
description:
Re-scoped 2026-09-17 to the decision on the one gate list (target architecture, docs/architecture/target-architecture.md, §9.1 D-10 and §9.3 O-4).

What: this repository's single list of gates becomes a platform-neutral gate file plus one `verify` command that runs it — developers and CI run the same command. CI does not enumerate gates on its own: `ci.yml` is derived from the gate file, either as one verify step or as one job per gate with a check that reports drift between the two. The CI helper (scripts/ci_gates.py) becomes that derivation instead of being the source. Portfolio later migrates its own CI steps into the same schema (its own item there); the two-reader adapter is a transition only.

Gate-file schema (O-4): lakeswitch-ai's gates.yaml schema as the basis; `entry` for the command, the field name pre-commit uses; enforcement as a closed vocabulary advisory / report / block; `floor` as the non-negotiable set; a `mutation_test` per gate; `schedule` and `reason` for reporting gates. No third format — a pre-commit file may be generated from the same list.

First gates: pytest and ruff (the kit keeps both, D-6); the Leerprobe as kit-probe, which portfolio dropped and which becomes this repository's acceptance gate; the export identity gate of D-4, together with the one script that renders .beads/issues.jsonl at session end (auto-export is already off since 2026-09-17).
acceptance_criteria:
- `verify` runs every gate of the gate file locally and exits non-zero on a blocking failure.
- ci.yml is derived; the drift check goes red on a hand-edited ci.yml.
- Every gate has a known-bad case that turns it red, and asserts a non-empty subject set.
- The export script writes .beads/issues.jsonl; its identity gate goes red when the export and the database disagree.
- The 27 red test_ci cases are green or reclassified with a reason (coding-harness-2ee).
notes:
Measured 2026-09-16 after the mechanism adoption (5efe809): 167 passed, 60 failed, 4 skipped; test_kit's 19 collected, not run (the Leerprobe is heavy). Red classes: 27 test_ci (this bead's scope), 21 test_regelwerk (rules at level 3+ name enforcers that stayed in portfolio as bestand), 11 test_feedback_channel, 1 test_model_endpoints (reads .claude/agents - Naht 1).
Correction (review of coding-harness PR #1): the full run without the test_kit exclusion is 64 failed / 182 passed / 4 skipped; 167/60/4 holds only with tests/test_kit.py excluded. The four red kit tests: test_every_tracked_file_has_a_role, test_the_kit_list_is_not_derivable_from_the_export_list, test_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere, test_the_role_check_goes_red_when_a_rule_is_removed.
2026-09-19: gate file (decisions/gates.yaml, 12 gates), canonical verifier (ci_gates.py reads it, validates schema, derives ci.yml, ci-drift holds), runner (verify_all.sh, no own commands, pinned interpreter, enforcement vocabulary), Makefile (make verify), three new checks (docs, bead-export, dangling-beads) with mutation proofs. make verify runs end to end: 9 green, pytest red on the 37 known 2ee failures, docs-links/markdownlint report-only. Export renderer of D-4 still outstanding — bead stays open.
2026-09-19 (2): D-4 delivered — scripts/render_beads_export.py (one-writer renderer, validates lines before writing) + the export-identity gate (committed export must equal the fresh render; SKIPs visibly where the tracker does not live). AGENTS.md rule 4 updated. With this, bo0's scope is complete — closes when PR #11 reaches main.

title: Change-artefact validator as a kit entry: class, Definition of Done, design artefact (D-11, D-12, D-14)
description:
Decided 2026-09-16 (target architecture, docs/architecture/target-architecture.md, §9.1 D-11, D-12, D-14 and §9.3 O-1): the validator that checks a change's artefacts for presence becomes a mechanism entry of this kit. It stayed in portfolio as an inventory file (validate_change_artefacts.py there); without it, phases 2 and 3 have no machine gate wherever the kit is copied.

Rules it carries or gains:
- spec.md exists for every change and carries `class` in its frontmatter, one of Spike, Bounded, Feature, Architectural (D-12).
- spec.md has a Definition of Done section whose gate line reads exactly "`verify` green" — one line, never a list (O-1).
- Class Architectural requires design.md with an ADR draft; class Feature requires design.md or a one-sentence reason in spec.md why not; Bounded and Spike need none (D-14).

The templates these rules check are built in the template bundle (coding-harness-9qo); the validator enters the gate file (coding-harness-bo0).
acceptance_criteria:
- The validator and its tests live in this repository; the kit manifest lists it as a mechanism entry.
- Every rule above has a known-bad case that turns the validator red.
- The Leerprobe runs it green in an empty repository.

title: Per-instance model routing file with schema and endpoint check (D-16)
description:
Decided 2026-09-16 (target architecture, docs/architecture/target-architecture.md, §9.1 D-16, §6.6 and principle P16): the doctrine names what a phase needs — much input and little reasoning, the highest reasoning, a reliable worker, a reviewer from another lineage — and never which model. Each instance carries a routing file (model-routing.yaml) that maps phase requirement to model to endpoint. The schema ships in the kit. One test resolves every entry against the endpoint declaration (model-endpoints.yaml); an entry that does not resolve is BLOCK, the same rule as RB-A6. The Anthropic-only stage-1 configuration ships as the example.

Follow-ups outside this item: the shell profiles read the file once they move here from portfolio; WORKFLOW.md drops its vendor names when it is rewritten.
acceptance_criteria:
- The schema, an example routing file and the test exist here.
- The test goes red on an entry whose model or endpoint is not declared.
- The kit manifest classifies the schema and test as mechanism and the routing file as scaffold.

title: Corpus correction pull request: mechanical fixes and one stage vocabulary (D-1, D-8)
description:
Decided 2026-09-16 (target architecture, docs/architecture/target-architecture.md, §9.1 D-1 and D-8): the research corpus under docs/research/ is corrected in place, in one pull request. The review of the corpus against the running workflow (docs/research/2026-09-16-review-corpus-vs-running-workflow.md) found mechanical errors and five different meanings of "stage" ("Stufe") across the documents.

Mechanical corrections: dates, images, ADR prefixes, the language line, the CVE attribution.

One vocabulary, corpus included:
- Stage 1–3 — model routing
- Setup step S0–S7
- Team level T0–T2
- Omnigent adoption M0–M4
- Enforcement level 1–5

The review document itself proposes team levels T0–T4; it is corrected to T0–T2 in the same pull request. Content findings are not corrected here — they stay beside the sources, in the review. Until the pull request merges, the research index (docs/research/_INDEX.md) carries the vocabulary table.
acceptance_criteria:
- One pull request carries all mechanical corrections and all renames.
- Every stage-like term in docs/research/ uses one of the five vocabularies above.
- No content finding of the review is silently changed; the diff is mechanical.

title: Public readiness: Apache-2.0 licence, onboarding page, denylist gate (D-17)
description:
Decided 2026-09-16 (target architecture, docs/architecture/target-architecture.md, §1.1, constraint C8 and §9.1 D-17): this repository becomes a public template that strangers clone. Three things start now, not at the template switch:
- A LICENSE file with Apache-2.0, the licence lakeswitch-ai uses.
- docs/onboarding.md: a stranger's path from the README to a first Bounded change (phases 4, 5 and 7) in one afternoon, with no question the pages leave unanswered (quality scenario Q13). Linked from the README.
- A denylist scan as a kit gate: no customer, employer or vendor name anywhere in the harness; vendor names only in an instance's routing configuration. It builds on the scan lakeswitch-ai already runs, enters the gate file (coding-harness-bo0), and must neither publish the denied names itself nor flag the documents that describe the rule.

The template switch is a separate event with its own conditions: Leerprobe at 95 % or more in both instances, the stage-2 entry runs measured, and Q13 passed once by someone who was not there.
acceptance_criteria:
- LICENSE (Apache-2.0) is present.
- docs/onboarding.md exists and the README links to it.
- The denylist gate is in the gate list, goes red on a known-bad case, and is green on main.
notes: 2026-09-17: depends on the gate file (coding-harness-bo0) because the denylist gate enters it. The licence and the onboarding page do not wait for it and can start at any time.

title: Adopt the five workflow-entry tests from portfolio once the entry exists here
description:
Portfolio's severance pull request (portfolio #162) deleted nine test functions that exist nowhere in this repository. Decided 2026-09-17 at session end: split them.

- The four human-gate tests read a portfolio artefact (its run-log schema). They are recorded in portfolio as a loss, in its ADR-032 — not rebuilt here.
- The five workflow-entry tests check the entry into a change: the start command and the make target that create a change folder. They belong with that entry and are adopted here once this repository has it. Today the change-folder script is present here (scripts/new_change.py); the start command and the make target are not.

Source of the five: portfolio master before the severance, its workflow-entry test file.
acceptance_criteria:
- The five tests exist here and are green against this repository's entry, or each deviation is rewritten with its reason.
- Portfolio's ADR-032 names this item as the new home of the five and records the four as lost.
